criterion_notes.c1: Does not examine household or community water or sanitation service access. Instead, the study frames and analyses municipal wastewater treatment plant operation at the municipality level as an environmental pollution-abatement measure to reduce untreated effluent discharges.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 reading: Under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2, this paper would pass Criterion 2 (plain=yes) because it examines inter-municipal policy diffusion/spillovers and models institutional and governance variables—specifically municipal water corporatization via creation of a public water enterprise (WaterEnterprise), female representation in municipal administration (Femadmin), and federal state policy affiliation (StateBelonging). Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, however, it fails Criterion 2 (narrow=no): the primary exposure is spatial proximity/spillovers of environmental pollution abatement across municipalities, and although WaterEnterprise reflects utility organizational form as a proxy for institutional quality, neither exposure examines a rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community water or sanitation service access (and overall plain_criterion2_decision remains exclude because Criteria 1 and 4 also fail).
criterion_notes.c3: Contains quantitative empirical evidence using secondary 2010 data across 2,299 Mexican municipalities analysed via general probit, spatial autoregressive (SAR) probit, and spatial Durbin probit models.
criterion_notes.c4: No household or community access, connection, service availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion outcome is reported. The sole dependent variable (wt) is a binary municipality-level indicator of whether any municipal wastewater treatment plant operated in 2010 (pollution abatement).
criterion_notes.c5: Unit of analysis and sample (2,299 Mexican municipalities in 2010), exposures (spatial lag of neighbouring municipalities' wastewater treatment and socioeconomic, demographic, and institutional controls), outcome (binary municipal wastewater treatment indicator wt), and cross-sectional spatial econometric design are clearly specified.

evidence_quotes.quote: As an example for an environmental measure we take wastewater treatment in Mexican municipalities.
We rely on cross-sectional data to investigate whether wastewater treatment takes place in a municipality.
In our sample of 2299 Mexican municipalities, 1526 or 66.4% of the municipalities did not treat wastewater in 2010 whereas the remaining 773 municipalities had plants that operated in 2010.
The dependent variable assumes a value of one if treatment takes place. Otherwise, it is zero.
As a proxy for institutional quality, we include the dummy variable “WaterEnterprise”. It assumes the value of one if a public water enterprise exists in a municipality. Otherwise, it is zero.

raw_response.exposure: Spatial lag of municipal wastewater treatment in k-nearest neighbouring municipalities (spatial spillovers), alongside socioeconomic, demographic, and institutional variables including existence of a municipal public water enterprise (WaterEnterprise), female share in municipal administration (Femadmin), and federal state affiliation (StateBelonging)
raw_response.outcome: Binary municipal-level indicator (wt) equal to 1 if wastewater treatment took place in the municipality in 2010 (at least one operating municipal wastewater treatment plant) and 0 otherwise
raw_response.population_and_sample: 2,299 Mexican municipalities in 2010 (out of 2,456 Mexican municipalities; municipality is the unit of analysis)
raw_response.rationale: Excluded (E01: Wrong topic). This spatial econometric study investigates environmental pollution abatement—specifically whether spatial spillovers across neighbouring municipalities explain whether a Mexican municipality operated a wastewater treatment plant in 2010 (wt = 1 vs. 0). It does not examine household or community water or sanitation service access (failing Criterion 1) and reports no outcome measuring household/community access, connection, reliability, continuity, affordability, or exclusion (failing Criterion 4). While it includes institutional governance controls that satisfy the plain wording of Criterion 2 (notably municipal utility corporatization via WaterEnterprise), it also fails the narrow 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 reading because no rule-type mechanism governing household or community service access is analysed; even under the plain Criterion 2 reading, the study remains excluded due to Criteria 1 and 4.
raw_response.study_design: Cross-sectional spatial econometric study (probit, spatial autoregressive probit, and spatial Durbin probit models)
